title: Any access to a decoy service
rationale: Green users never use decoys (CAGE-4 README, Deception), so any access is an unambiguous Red signal.

title: Connection to SSH service port
rationale: In 3 dumped CAGE-4 episodes about 92% of well-known-port events were port 22 (exploit attempts and scans); green users also use it.

title: New process created by a service daemon
rationale: A successful exploit shows up natively as a bare process record (PID only); the bridge adds the parent, so a daemon parent is the signal.

title: Elevated process on a host
rationale: Privilege escalation (PrivilegeEscalate) is rare in normal green work.

title: Shell started by a service daemon
rationale: Exploited services typically spawn a shell; the parent name heuristic can also match benign daemons.

title: Probe of common remote-access ports
rationale: Service discovery touches remote-access ports; green traffic also uses them, so expect false positives.

title: Web service port probe
rationale: Weak signal on its own: green users browse. Logged for correlation only.

title: Connection into a restricted zone
rationale: Restricted zones carry mission-critical traffic; unusual sources deserve a look but this alone is noisy.

title: Service stopped or degraded
rationale: Impact (T1489 Service Stop) and DegradeServices show up as service events.

title: Elevated process under a network service parent
rationale: Escalation directly under a daemon suggests an exploited service.
